sections.title: Introduction
sections.text: The Tempest plugins can be used from other plugins (Java) and from content mods that have no code (JSON assets). Core is the base: everything shared is in com.atomictempest.core (events, leaderboards, help, settings, HUD lines, perks, and the economy bridge). Each plugin has its own small api package. Plugin Manifest id API Core AtomicTempest:Core com.atomictempest.core ( economy.Economies , events, leaderboards, help, settings, HUD lines, perks) Coins AtomicTempest:Coins com.atomictempest.coins.api.CoinsAPI (what only Coins has), CoinStacks Quests AtomicTempest:Quests com.atomictempest.quests

sections.title: Server guide
sections.text: The pages in this section are made from the plugins themselves: the commands, the /tempest settings with their explanations, and the /guide pages players read. They say exactly what the game says.

sections.title: Install
sections.text: Put Tempest Core in your server's mods folder. Every other Tempest plugin needs it. Put the plugins you want next to it. Each one works on its own; together they connect (quests count crates, events boost the shop, jobs pay more for what contracts want, and so on). Money comes from Tempest Economy (Coins) , or from any economy plugin through VaultUnlocked. Start the server. Each plugin makes its files under universe/mods with safe defaults.

sections.text: Command Who What it opens /tempest Admins Every setting of every Tempest plugin, one tab each, with a search box. sections.title: Free and Pro
sections.text: Some plugins come as a free jar and a Pro jar with the same name. The Pro jar replaces the free one and keeps everything the server made. Free limits only stop you making more: they never break what a server already has. Core, Economy and the plugins' APIs are always free.

sections.title: Saving, backups and networks
sections.text: Everything is saved in files by default, safely through crashes and power cuts, with a backup every 12 hours. With a Pro plugin, several servers can share one economy and players' progress through a MySQL or MariaDB database. See Saving and backups , Database and server networks and Big servers .

sections.title: Languages
sections.text: Every text players see is in 8 languages (English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian). Players get their game's language when Tempest has it; the server-wide language is in /tempest → General. With a Pro plugin installed, /tempest texts lets you reword any text.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.text: Coins are the money on this server. You earn them, keep them in your wallet, and spend them on what the server offers. Your balance: 12,901 copper. What the coins are worth Every price is counted in copper. The other coins are worth: Coin Iron5,Coin Silver10,Coin Gold50,Coin Emerald100,Coin Diamond500 On this server -Wallet and ATM -Earning coins -Daily rewards -Money counter -Shared banks -Crates -Leaderboards -Shop -Quests and achievements -Slot machines -Lottery -Coinflip -Server events -Battle pass -Contracts -Jobs -Trade -Land claims -Town -Town projects Pick a page on the left to read more. Open this screen any time with /coins. Admins also read: Your balance: 24,800 copper.

sections.title: Wallet and ATM
sections.text: Your wallet Coins in your wallet are safe. Coins you carry as items are not: you can drop or lose them like anything else in your bags. Open your wallet with /wallet (or /bal), or at any ATM. Taking coins out Each coin in the wallet has buttons to take out 1, 10 or 100 of it. Putting coins in Press "Put all my coins in" to put every coin you carry into your wallet. You can also hold a coin and right-click. Paying someone Press "Pay a player" in the wallet and pick someone who is online, or type /pay <player> <amount>. History The bottom of the wallet shows your latest gains and spending. ATMs An ATM opens the same wallet, and pays out with a shower of coins. ATMs are shown on your map. Only admins can build ATMs on this server. Admins also read: Your rank perks: VIP Daily rewards +100% Shop prices -15% Shop sell prices +10% Payment fee -100% Quest rewards +50%

sections.title: Earning coins
sections.text: Fighting Creatures you defeat drop coins. The tougher the creature, the more it drops. Mining Ores sometimes drop coins when you mine them. Rarer ores drop more: Copper Ore: 10% chance of 1 copper Iron Ore: 10% chance of 2 copper Silver Ore: 15% chance of 5 copper Gold Ore: 15% chance of 10 copper Cobalt Ore: 20% chance of 20 copper Mithril Ore: 25% chance of 50 copper Adamantite Ore: 30% chance of 100 copper Thorium Ore: 20% chance of 30 copper Onyxium Ore: 25% chance of 60 copper Ores that players placed give no coins. Every day Claim a free reward once a day with /daily. Come back on following days for bigger rewards. Selling Sell items you do not need at a shop stall. See the Shop page. Luck Try the slot machines or the lottery for a big win, but over time luck costs more than it pays. Other players Trade with other players and pay each other with /pay or the wallet.

sections.title: Daily rewards
sections.text: Your reward for day 1 is ready! Open the calendar to claim it. How it works Claim once a day with /daily. Each day in a row moves you along the calendar to a bigger reward. Miss a day and you start again from day 1. After day 7 the calendar starts over. The rewards Day 1: 50 copper Day 2: 60 copper Day 3: 70 copper Day 4: 80 copper Day 5: 100 copper Day 6: 120 copper Day 7: 250 copper

sections.title: Shared banks
sections.text: Saving up together A shared bank holds coins for a group: a town, a team, friends saving for something big. Open one with /bank (it costs 500 copper) and add your friends by name. Who can do what Everyone in the bank can put coins in. Only the owner, and members the owner allows, can take coins out. The history shows who put in and took out what. Closing Members can leave whenever they like. When the owner closes the bank, whatever is in it goes to the owner. Your banks Steves_Team: 1,000 copper

Copper go into your wallet. Every crate card shows its rarest prize and its chance. Some crates have a pity: after so many opens in a row without an Epic or better prize, the next one is always Epic or better. The card shows how close you are. Win a Epic prize or better and the whole server hears about it.

sections.title: Quests and achievements
sections.text: Achievements Goals for the whole time you play, like mining 100 ores or hitting the jackpot. They count by themselves, and each pays a reward once. Some are secret until you find them. Quests Pick quests from the quest board in /quests: you can do 3 at a time. Daily and weekly quests come back when they reset, so you can earn them again. Quest journal Every finished quest and achievement gives quest points: your rank grows from Wanderer to Legend, and higher ranks earn more from quests. sections.title: Slot machines
sections.text: How to play Walk up to a slot machine and press F. Each spin takes your bet from your wallet; line up three of the same symbol to win. Your bet Crouch and press F on a machine, or type /slotbet, to choose your bet: 10, 50, 100 or 500 copper. Yours is 10 right now. Every prize below is your bet times the payout, so a bigger bet wins bigger. What three of a kind pay Three cherries: 2 times your bet Three bells: 4 times your bet Three coins: 6 times your bet Three diamonds: 16 times your bet The jackpot Three sevens win the jackpot: 10 times your bet plus the whole pot, which is 500 copper right now. Part of every lost spin goes into the pot, so it keeps growing until someone wins it. Bet 500 to win the whole pot. A smaller bet wins a share: 10 wins 2% of it. Your winnings Winnings come out of the machine as coins. For 90 seconds only you can pick them up; after that, anyone can. Good to know A machine takes one spin at a time. If someone else is spinning, wait for the reels to stop. The machines are a game of luck. Some spins win big, but over many spins they pay back less than you put in. Only admins can build slot machines on this server.

sections.title: Coinflip
sections.text: How it works Make a room: pick a stake and a side, heads or tails. Your stake is held while the room is open. Another player joins with the same stake on the other side. The coin flips, and the winner takes the pot. Stakes from 10 copper to 1,000,000 copper. A room nobody joins closes after 30 min and the stake comes back. If the server restarts, open rooms close and their stakes come back. A coin already in the air is paid out. Provably fair Every room has a secret seed from the start. Its SHA-256 is shown while the room is open, so it cannot be changed later. After the flip the seed is shown. The roll is the first 13 hex digits of SHA-256(seed:room id) divided by 16^13; under 0.5 is heads. You Won 1, lost 2. Profit: +850 copper (staked 2,150 copper in all). Admins also read: Won 2, lost 1. Profit: -850 copper (staked 2,150 copper in all).

sections.title: Saving and backups
sections.text: Every Tempest plugin saves in files under universe/mods . This is the default, it needs no setup, and it is safe for big servers on Windows and Linux. A database (MySQL or MariaDB) is only needed when several servers share one economy: see Database and server networks .

sections.title: How a save stays safe
sections.text: A save can be cut off at any moment: a crash, a power cut, a host that kills the server. The plugins never write over the old file directly, so a save is either fully done or not done at all. The new text goes to name.tmp and is flushed to the disk. The old file becomes name.bak . The new file takes its place in one step. When a file is read, the plugins use the newest complete copy. A file that cannot be read is kept as name.broken-<time> (so nothing is ever thrown away) and the backup copy is used instead. Danger What the plugins do A crash or power cut in the middle of a save The old file or the .bak copy is still whole. The next start uses it Two saves of the same file at the same moment Saves and reads of one file never overlap. The newest data always wins Windows: a virus scanner, backup tool or sync program has the file open The save waits a moment and tries again, instead of failing Linux: the disk loses the new name after a power cut The folder is synced too, so the new file is really on the disk A server stopping while saving The save still finishes. A stop cannot cut a file in half A file edited by hand with a mistake It is kept as name.broken-<time> , the last good copy is used, and the error is logged Two server processes on the same folder Found and named to admins (see below) What a crash can lose. Rewards, purchases and claims are saved before they are given, so a crash never gives anything twice. Routine progress is saved every few seconds (money about every

sections.title: Backups
sections.text: The plugins make a backup of all Tempest data every 12 hours. Backups are free and work with files and with a database. Each backup is a zip file in universe/tempest-backups with: the files of all Tempest plugins ( universe/mods/... ), but no jar files and never the database password; with a database: each shared table as text ( database/<table>.jsonl ); about.txt : when, why, and how to restore. Setting ( /tempest → Saving) Default What it does Hours between backups 12 0 to 168. 0 turns automatic backups off Backups kept 14 1 to 1000. The oldest Tempest backups are deleted, nothing else Backup folder universe/tempest-backups A folder in the server folder, or a full path such as D:/backups/tempest Back up the database too On The shared tables go into each backup Back up the network money log too Off The money log of all servers. It can be large These settings work at once, with no restart. Make a backup now: /tempest backup . It also lists the newest backups. A full disk never breaks the server. A backup is not made if it would leave less than 512 MB free, because the plugins need room to save. Admins get a message in game (and on Discord, if Coins' Discord alerts are set up). Keep fewer backups, or move the backup folder to another disk. Backups are private. They never contain the database password. On Linux only the server's own user can read them. They do contain every player's data and the network's seal.key , so keep the backup folder as private as the server itself.

sections.title: Restore a backup
sections.text: Stop the server. Open the zip and copy files/universe/mods over the server's universe/mods . If you save in a database, type the password again in /tempest → Saving (or use env:NAME ). Start the server.

sections.title: Good habits
sections.text: Put the backup folder on a different disk, or in a folder that a sync program copies somewhere else. Follow the 3-2-1 rule: 3 copies of the data, on 2 kinds of storage, 1 copy in another place. With a database, also turn on your database host's own backups (for example automated backups with point-in-time recovery). On a network, one server that backs up the database is enough: turn "Back up the database too" off on the others.

sections.title: One server process per folder
sections.text: Only one server process may use a server folder. Some hosting panels can start the same server twice after a crash or a restart, and two processes writing the same files would lose data. The plugins notice this. The second process names the first one in its log, and every admin gets a message in game and on Discord: "Another server process is using this server's folder". The message repeats every 10 minutes until one of the two is stopped. Stop one of them.

sections.title: Is file saving enough for a big server?
sections.text: Yes, for one server. The safe-save steps above are tested on Windows and on Linux, including saves cut off half way and saves on a server that is stopping. You need a database only when: two or more servers must share one economy and players' progress, or a website, a bot or another tool must read the data while the server runs. See Big servers for the load tests with hundreds of players.

sections.title: Database and server networks
sections.text: By default every server keeps its own data in files ( Saving and backups ). With a database, two or more servers can share it: a player who earns 500 coins on your survival server has them on your lobby and minigame servers too, with the same battle pass tiers, quests and jobs. Use a database when: two or more servers must share one economy, and players' progress must follow them; or a website, a bot or a backup tool must read the data of a server. A database needs any Tempest Pro plugin on each server. Saving in files, backups and everything on Saving and backups are free.

sections.title: What the servers can share
sections.text: You choose each part in /tempest → Saving. Parts you do not share stay in each server's own files. Part What follows the player Money (shared wallets) Balance, stats, daily streak, the last changes. Banks stay on each server Battle pass XP, claimed tiers, premium Quests Quests, achievements, progress, rerolls Jobs The jobs the player holds, level and XP of each job, today's pay, explorer places Leaderboards for the whole network The Pass, Quests and Jobs boards rank the players of all servers One money log for the whole network Every money change on every server, in one log ( /eco network log ) All parts are on when you turn the database on. The money boards (richest, top earners) rank all servers when money is shared. These always stay on each server: server quests, the paid places of a quest (first 5 players), the player limit of a job, shared banks, crates, shops, holograms, the lottery and coinflip rooms.

sections.title: No dupes: one owner server at a time
sections.text: The hard part of a network is that a player can switch servers in a second. If two servers could change the same wallet, a player could spend the same coins twice, or claim the same reward on each server. The plugins prevent this. Each player's data has one owner server at a time : the server the player is on. When a player joins, that server takes their data from the database. If the previous server still holds it, the new server waits. The player sees "Your wallet is on its way" or a similar message. This usually takes less than a second. While the player plays, the owner server saves their data. Before it gives a reward or money, it saves and waits until the database has it. When the player leaves, the owner server saves the data and lets it go. A server that does not own a player's data changes nothing for them and gives no rewards for it. So a reward claimed on one server can never be claimed again on another. If a server crashes without letting go, its players' data is free again after 1 minute. Its last save counts. Money to a player on another server. /pay , shop sales and other payments go to the owner server, which adds them. /pay <name> <amount> finds the player on any server of the network, and they see the payment on their server. If the player is offline everywhere, the database is changed directly. Every change carries a code, so it is never counted twice, even if a server crashes halfway.

sections.title: When the database goes down
sections.text: A database can stop: an outage at the cloud host, a restart, a network problem. The servers keep running and no player is kicked. Time What players can do What waits The first 30 seconds Everything Nothing. The servers keep the changes and save them when the database is back After 30 seconds Earn money, get pass XP, make quest progress, do jobs (with pay) Spending money (shops, /pay , crates), claiming pass tiers, quest rewards. Players see "The money server cannot be reached right now. Your coins are safe" A player who joins during the outage Earn money (it is added when the database is back) Spending, and their pass, quests and jobs: "on its way" When the database is back Everything Nothing. Every change goes into the database exactly once Spending waits after 30 seconds on purpose: after 60 seconds another server may take over a wallet, and the same coins must never be spent twice. If a server restarts while the database is down, it keeps what changed. Coins keeps every money change in universe/mods/coins/network-outbox.json ; Pass, Quests and Jobs keep their files up to date and Core remembers which players' progress the database does not have yet. When the database is back, it all goes in. If another server changed the same player in the meantime, the database counts. Admins are told. sections.title: Snapshots and rollback
sections.text: With a database, the plugins keep snapshots of each player: a few seconds after they leave a server, and whenever an admin runs /tempest snapshot <player> . A snapshot holds the player's shared wallet, battle pass, quests and jobs. To put a player back to an earlier state (after a scam, a bug or a mistake): Run /tempest snapshots <player> . The list shows the number, time and reason of each snapshot. Make sure the player is offline on every server. Run /tempest rollback <player> <number> . The player now has that snapshot's data on every server. First, the plugins keep a pinned "before rollback" snapshot, so a rollback can always be undone: roll back to that one. A rollback never runs while the player is online anywhere: the plugins never change data a server is using. With tamper seals on, a snapshot that was changed in the database is refused.

sections.title: A database with a standby copy (failover)
sections.text: A cloud database with automatic failover (for example Amazon RDS Multi-AZ, or DigitalOcean with standby nodes): use its one address. The host moves the address to the standby. Your own database servers that always hold the same data (Galera, or synchronous replication): type every address in "Address", with commas: db1.example.com,db2.example.com . The plugins use the first one that answers. Do not use a replica that runs behind the main database (asynchronous replication): players could get old money and progress from it.

sections.title: Tamper seals
sections.text: Anyone who can write to the database (a leaked password, a staff member with a database panel, a website) could change numbers in it. Tamper seals catch this. A seal is a code that only a server with the seal key can make, and the key is in the servers' files, not in the database. Run /eco network seal on on one server. If it says "Not yet", copy universe/mods/coins/seal.key from this server to each server it names. They read it within 10 seconds, no restart needed. Run /eco network seal on again. It should say "Seals are on". Copy seal.key to each new server before it joins the network. What was changed in the database What happens A wallet The wallet is frozen: the player can earn but not spend. Admins are told in game and on Discord A money change between servers It is refused and deleted. Nobody's money changes A pass, quest or job record It is not used. The player's progress waits. Admins are told Then run /eco network tampered to see what changed. /eco network accept <player> keeps the change (if it was yours); /eco network restore <player> takes back only that change, and money the player earned after it stays. Keep seal.key secret: anyone with it can make seals that fit. A server without the right key waits instead of writing data nobody can check.

sections.title: Turning a part off, or the database off
sections.text: You can turn one part off, or the whole database, at any time, and on again later. Players lose no progress and nobody can claim a reward twice. Off: at the next start, the server copies the newest data of that part from the database into its files (with money players got while away), after a backup of the wallet files. Then it runs from files. On again: players who only played here while it was off keep this server's data. Players another server changed in the meantime keep the database's data; they are listed in universe/mods/coins/network-conflicts.csv , and the backup has this server's amount. Remove a server from the network: run /eco network download (it should say "wallets written"), turn off "Save in a database", and restart.

sections.title: How it stays fast
sections.text: Nothing waits on the game thread. Earning money, pass XP and quest progress never wait for the disk or the database, so the world never stutters because of a save. Saves are grouped. On a network, routine saves of all players go to the database together, about once a second, in one go. 300 players cost about as much as a few. Only rewards wait. Before a reward or money is given, its save is confirmed. This is what makes dupes impossible. Files are saved safely and in the background. See Saving and backups .

sections.title: Setting up a big server
sections.text: One server: files are enough. Turn on backups to another disk (they are on by default, every 12 hours). A network: Put the database in the same region or data centre as the game servers. Under 5 ms is best. A database far away works, but players wait longer when they join or switch servers, and finishing a quest can wait up to 2 seconds. Use MySQL 8.4+ or MariaDB 10.11+, with a database user that has rights on the Tempest database only. For a database with a standby copy, see failover . Let one server back up the database; turn "Back up the database too" off on the others, and turn on your database host's own backups. Set up Coins' Discord alerts, so you hear about database outages and failed backups at once. Turn on tamper seals if anyone besides the servers can write to the database.

sections.title: Known limits
sections.text: With a database far away (tens of milliseconds), two things are slower. Neither loses anything; players only wait. Situation What players notice Many players joining in the same second (after a restart) Their wallet and progress can take several seconds to arrive ("on its way") Finishing a quest Up to 2 seconds before the reward is given A database in the same region as the game servers has neither. Both are being improved.

sections.title: Checklist
sections.text: Step What to do 1 Put Tempest Core (and the plugins you use) in your server's mods folder, and compile against their jars with compileOnly 2 Depend on AtomicTempest:Core in your manifest.json ; make the other Tempest plugins optional 3 Make one Registrations for your plugin and close() it in shutdown() 4 Ask Core for what you need on every use ( Economies.get() , Levels.get() ): mods can start after yours 5 Before using anything newer than the Core you support, check CoreAPI.runningVersion()

sections.title: 1. Compile against the jars
sections.text: Download the jars from the plugins' CurseForge pages, then in build.gradle : groovy Copy dependencies { compileOnly(files("libs/Core-1.5.0.jar")) compileOnly(files("libs/Quests-1.4.0.jar")) // only if you use it } compileOnly means the jars are not packed into yours: the server loads them from its mods folder.

sections.title: 2. Declare the dependencies
sections.text: json Copy "Dependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" }, "OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Coins": "*", "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" } Note With an optional dependency, check that the plugin is there ( QuestsAPI.isAvailable() , CoinsAPI.get() != null ) and touch its classes in one class of yours only, so your plugin still loads without it.

sections.title: 3. Register with Core
sections.text: java Copy public class DragonsPlugin extends JavaPlugin { private final Registrations core = new Registrations("Dragons"); public DragonsPlugin(JavaPluginInit init) { super(init); } @Override protected void setup() { core.placeholder("dragons_slain", uuid -> String.valueOf(slain(uuid))); core.onAction((player, action, amount) -> { if (action.equals(PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN)) { /* a crate was opened */ } }); } @Override public void shutdown() { core.close(); // takes back everything registered above super.shutdown(); } }

sections.title: 4. Pay a player, read their level
sections.text: java Copy Economy money = Economies.get(); // null while no economy is installed if (money != null) { money.deposit(player, 250, "Dragons: a dragon slain"); // the reason shows in the economy log } Levels.Leveling leveling = Levels.get(); // Endless Leveling or MMO Skill Tree, or null if (leveling != null && leveling.level(player) >= 20) { leveling.giveXp(player, 100, "Dragons: a dragon slain"); }

sections.title: 5. Check the Core version
sections.text: java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 19 && Skills.available()) { int mining = Skills.level(player, "Mining"); // MMO Skill Tree skills (API 19) } Tip Keep code that needs a newer Core in a class of its own and call it only after the check: on an older Core the class is then never loaded, and your plugin keeps working. Next: Setting up a plugin has every option, and Player actions lists everything the Tempest plugins report.

sections.title: Link your mod to Tempest
sections.text: You make a leveling, party, claims or gameplay mod and want it to work with the whole Tempest suite (quests, the battle pass, events, jobs, crates, the shop, rewards, the board). You do not need to add support for sixteen plugins: you talk to Tempest Core once, and every Tempest plugin sees it. Everything here is optional for you and for the server: declare Core as an optional dependency, check that it runs, and your mod works the same without it. json Copy "OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" } java Copy boolean tempest = CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 14; // Core is there and new

sections.title: A leveling mod: your levels in the whole suite
sections.text: Implement Levels.Leveling and register it. From then on Tempest's level rewards, level and class limits on shop items, crates and quests, "reach level" quests, battle pass XP, the level board and Tempest's own XP (jobs, quests, crates, contracts, projects) all use your mod. java Copy final class TempestLink implements Levels.Leveling { public String name() { return "My Leveling"; } public int level(UUID player) { return MyLeveling.level(player); } public int prestige(UUID player) { return 0; } // 0 when your mod has none public boolean giveXp(UUID player, double amount, String reason) { // Tempest giving your XP return MyLeveling.addXp(player, amount); // with your own bonuses and cap } // Optional, all with defaults: xp, xpForNext, levelCap, playerClass, secondClass, race, classTier, mobLevel, inPartyWith } // In setup() or start(), while Core runs: TempestLink link = new TempestLink(); Levels.register(link); // In shutdown(): Levels.unregister(link); Tell Tempest when a player levels up (once per level-up, even when several levels were crossed): java Copy Levels.fireLevelUp(uuid, oldLevel, newLevel); Levels.firePrestige(uuid, oldPrestige, newPrestige); // if your mod has prestige Your mod then shows by its name() in the admin's "Leveling mod" choice on the /tempest Leveling tab (Core API 21), next to Endless Leveling, RPG Leveling and MMO Skill Tree, which Core links by itself. So a server with several leveling mods picks the one that gives "the level". On "Automatic" a reg

sections.title: Any mod: count in quests, the pass and events
sections.text: Report what players do in your mod. Tempest Quests can turn any of these into a goal, and other Tempest plugins listen too: java Copy PlayerActions.fire(uuid, "mymod:boss_kill", 1); // your own name, "mod:what" QuestsAPI.trigger(uuid, "visit_shrine", 1); // a "Custom trigger" goal the admin made in /quests QuestsAPI belongs to Tempest Quests: declare "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" as an optional dependency too, and call it only when QuestsAPI.isAvailable() (the Quests page). Hear what players do in the Tempest plugins (a shop purchase, a quest finished, a job level, a crate opened), with the full list on the Player actions page: java Copy PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> { ... });

sections.title: Any mod: give party renown
sections.text: With Tempest Claims, every party has renown : a level that never drops and brings land and perks, and a season score for the "Most renowned parties" board. Your mod can give a player's party renown for something worth it (a boss, a dungeon, a rare find), and read the level to unlock your own things (API 26): java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() >= 26) { long got = Claims.addRenown(uuid, "mymod_dragon", 25); // what the party really got, 0 for none int level = Claims.renownLevel(uuid); // the party's level, 0 without a party } Claims decides, with the same rules as its own sources: the player must be in a party, past the new-member wait and really playing, and every mod's renown together stays inside a daily cap per member that the admin sets. Without Tempest Claims every call answers 0, so nothing needs a second path. Name your source in lower case ( mymod_dragon ): players read it on the party's renown page. When a party reaches a level, every member fires the claims_renown_level action (amount: the level), which PlayerActions.listen hears. The Land claims section of the Core page has the details.

sections.title: Money
sections.text: Use the server's economy, whichever plugin keeps it, through Economies.get() (the Money page). Tempest Economy also registers as VaultUnlocked's and Cassaforte's economy, so a mod that already uses those works with Tempest coins without any of this.

sections.title: Rewards, announcements, settings
sections.text: Want Use Page Give items safely (a full inventory goes to the mailbox) Rewards.giveItems Rewards, mail and boosts A big moment on the server's Discord (Tempest Economy posts it when Discord is set up) Announcements.post("mymod", text) Boards, HUD and placeholders A tab in the server's /tempest settings, with rows that show only when they mean something ( shownWhenOn ...) CasinoSettings.register(new SettingsTab(...)) Settings and menus Places on the world map MapPlaces Map, town and demand A line on the player's Tempest board HudLines Boards, HUD and placeholders

sections.title: Rules that keep servers safe
sections.text: Check CoreAPI.runningVersion() before using anything newer than the version you built against. Unregister everything you registered in shutdown() : servers reload plugins. Event listeners run on the thread that fired them: keep them quick; do world work with world.execute(...) . Never give money or items twice for one thing: Tempest's own rewards are saved before they are given; do the same. Questions or something missing: ask on our Discord. We add what mod authors need, and say so in API versions .

sections.title: Setting up a plugin
sections.text: Compile against the jars you use, without bundling them; the server loads them from Mods: groovy Copy dependencies { compileOnly(files("$hytaleHome/UserData/Mods/Core-1.0.0.jar")) compileOnly(files("$hytaleHome/UserData/Mods/Quests-1.1.0.jar")) // only if you use it } Download the jars from the plugins' CurseForge pages ( https://www.curseforge.com/hytale/mods/search?search=tempest ). In your manifest.json , depend on what you use so it starts before your plugin: json Copy "Dependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Core": "*" }, "OptionalDependencies": { "AtomicTempest:Coins": "*", "AtomicTempest:Quests": "*" } With an optional dependency, check CoinsAPI.get() != null or QuestsAPI.isAvailable() (or LotteryAPI.isAvailable() ...) before use, and keep the classes that touch it apart from the rest, so your plugin still loads when it is missing. Use the APIs in your plugin's setup() or later.

sections.title: The shortest way: Registrations and JsonFiles (Core)
sections.text: Registrations registers with Core's registries and remembers how to undo each one; one close() in shutdown() takes it all back, so a reload never leaves a settings tab, help page, listener or timer behind: java Copy private final Registrations core = new Registrations("Dragons"); protected void setup() { config = DragonsConfig.load(); core.settingsTab(new SettingsTab("Dragons", settings(config), config::save)); core.helpTopic(new HelpTopic("dragons", 80, Message.translation("server.dragons.help.title"), "Rock_Gem_Ruby", uuid -> lines(uuid))); core.helpCommand("server.dragons.help.mod", "/dragons", Message.translation("server.dragons.help.command")); core.hudLine("dragons.next", uuid -> Message.translation("server.dragons.hud.next")); core.placeholder("dragons_slain", uuid -> String.valueOf(slain(uuid))); core.mapKind(new MapPlaces.Kind("nest", "Dragon nests", Message.translation("server.dragons.map.nest")).blocks("Dragon_Nest"::equals)); core.leaderboard(board); core.onWallet(listener); core.veto(veto); core.onAction(listener); core.onAnnouncement(listener); core.restrictCraft("Dragon_Egg", () -> config.playersCanCraft()); core.edition(isPro, PRO_ADDS, licensedTo); // plugins with a free and a Pro jar core.every(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS, () -> spawnDragons()); // its own daemon timer thread; errors are logged core.later(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS, () -> greet()); core.onClose(() -> config.save()); // anything else for shutdown() } public void shutdown() { core.close(); // newest first;

sections.title: Which Core is installed: CoreAPI (Core)
sections.text: CoreAPI.runningVersion() is the API version of the Core on the server ( CoreAPI.API_VERSION is the one you compiled against; it is copied into your plugin, so ask runningVersion() at run time). Version 1 is Core 1.0.0. Core's stable API , safe to build on: the classes directly in com.atomictempest.core (except Main ) and the packages economy , help and settings . These only grow. Core's command , config , listener , player and ui packages and Main are internal and may change in any release; do not use them. The other plugins' APIs are their api packages ( Holograms.API_VERSION , QuestsAPI.API_VERSION , CoinsAPI.VERSION , CoinflipAPI.VERSION ...). java Copy if (CoreAPI.runningVersion() < 1) { /* a Core older than the one you built against */ }

sections.title: Reference: Core API versions
sections.text: CoreAPI.API_VERSION is the version a plugin was built against; CoreAPI.runningVersion() is the one installed on the server. Check the running version before touching anything newer than your lowest supported Core, and keep that code in a class of its own. Version Added 1 Core 1.0.0: Registrations , JsonFiles , Economies , CasinoSettings , HelpTopics , HudLines , Leaderboards , Placeholders , PlayerActions , WalletEvents and the rest of the first release 2 AdminLog , RateLimit , and settings tab groups ( tempest.admin.<group> ) 3 PlayLimits , HudLines.compact , Themes , dropdowns and item pickers in settings ( Setting.choice , Setting.item ), tab icons, ItemIcons.ids and pretty 4 The Tempest board's line names and keys ( HudLines.name , nameOf , keys , lineFor ) 5 Boosts and Registrations.boost ; PlayerActions.QUEST_COMPLETE and CONTRACT_DELIVER 6 Mailbox (/mail) and HudLines.startOff 7 MapPlaces and Registrations.mapKind 8 Unlocks and Registrations.unlockFeature , unlockProvider , onUnlock 9 Activity and Perks.highestPercent 10 Perks.Bonus.PASS_XP 11 SettingsTab.defaults (Reset to defaults) 12 JsonFiles config versions with migrations, and JsonFiles.rename 13 Doctor (/tempest doctor) and Registrations.doctor 14 Levels : player levels from a leveling mod 15 Levels dungeon, wave gate and raid clears; Boosts.LEVELING_XP 16 Levels XP, level cap, class, race, mob level, parties, raid starts, meets , hasClass , mobGold , mobKilled , playersAtLevel , serverClears , serverPrestige ;

sections.title: Money: Economies (Core)
sections.text: The server's money, whichever plugin keeps it: Coins when it is installed, otherwise any economy VaultUnlocked offers (Ecotale, TheEconomy, EliteEssentials...). Ask for it on every use: an economy can start after your plugin. java Copy Economy money = Economies.get(); // com.atomictempest.core.economy; null when there is none long balance = money.balance(uuid); money.deposit(uuid, 250, "Dragon bounty"); // false if refused; the reason shows in Coins' wallet history if (money.withdraw(uuid, 100, "Ferry ticket")) { /* paid */ } // false (nothing taken) if too little or vetoed money.has(uuid, 100); money.format(1250); // "1,250 copper", or "$1,250.00" from another economy Amounts are whole numbers of the economy's smallest unit (an economy with decimals shows balances rounded down). Always give a reason. withdraw asks the WalletEvents vetoes first, and every change through any economy reaches WalletEvents listeners. Coins the player holds as items are not in the wallet until deposited.

sections.title: Coins: CoinsAPI
sections.text: What only Coins has. CoinsAPI is also an Economy , so everything above works on it too. java Copy CoinsAPI coins = CoinsAPI.get(); // null when Coins is not installed coins.setBalance(uuid, 1000); // "Set by an admin" in the history coins.transfer(from, to, 50, "Trade"); // "Paid: Trade" / "Received: Trade" coins.paidAsCoins(uuid, 250, "Slot machine win"); // VERSION 4: you paid coin items instead of the wallet List<ItemStack> items = CoinStacks.of(1250); // coin items worth an amount, most valuable first // VERSION 5: shared banks (/bank) for other plugins CoinsAPI.BankView bank = coins.bank("Harbour"); // by name, or coins.bank(id); null when there is none coins.bankCanUse(bank.id(), player); // its owner or a member coins.bankCanWithdraw(bank.id(), player); // its owner, or a member the owner allows coins.bankDeposit(bank.id(), 120, "Taxes"); // coins your plugin already holds go in coins.bankWithdraw(bank.id(), 40, "Upkeep"); // coins come out for your plugin The bank's history shows your reason. Tempest Claims keeps a party's money in a bank this way, so it earns the bank's savings interest. Check CoinsAPI.VERSION >= 5 at compile time and catch LinkageError around these calls when your plugin may meet an older Coins. When your plugin pays out coin items instead of money (dropped, put in a tray), call paidAsCoins with the reason you would give a wallet change: the balance does not change, but the economy screen ( /eco ) and the leaderboards count the payout under its kind

sections.title: Stopping payments: WalletEvents.addVeto
sections.text: A veto is asked before coins leave a wallet (bets, crates, shop purchases, payments) and can refuse with a sentence for the player. Coins coming in cannot be refused, because the player may already have handed something over for them. java Copy WalletEvents.addVeto((uuid, amount, reason) -> jail.contains(uuid) ? "You cannot spend coins in jail." : null); String why = WalletEvents.checkRemoval(uuid, 100, "Ferry ticket"); // ask first to show the reason

sections.title: Player actions
sections.text: All in com.atomictempest.core , available whether or not Coins is installed.

sections.title: Hearing about money: WalletEvents and PlayerActions
sections.text: java Copy // Every change of any wallet (after it happened) WalletEvents.listen((player, amount, reason, balanceAfter) -> { ... }); // What players do in the economy mods: spins, wins, tickets, shop trades, daily rewards, payments PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> { if (PlayerActions.SLOT_JACKPOT.equals(action)) { ... } }); // Report your own (other listeners, such as Quests, may count them) PlayerActions.fire(uuid, "mymod:bounty", 250); Actions: slot_spin (bet), slot_win (winnings, also when dropped as coins), slot_jackpot , lottery_tickets (how many), lottery_win , shop_buy (cost), shop_sell (paid), daily_reward , pay , crate_open (price), coinflip_bet (stake), coinflip_win (paid), coinflip_loss (stake), quest_complete (reward paid; Core API 5, reported by Quests for every quest and achievement finished), contract_deliver (items delivered; Core API 5, reported by Contracts for every delivery to a server order), events_top (the place, 1 to 3, when an event ends), events_helped (a goal reached and the helper paid), trade_done (to each side of a finished trade that moved something; the amount is a number that always stands for the same other player), town_mayor (elected at the end of a term). Listeners run on the thread that made the change: keep them quick, and do world or UI work with world.execute(...) .

sections.title: Reference: every player action
sections.text: Everything the Tempest plugins report through PlayerActions (Core), in one place. Listen once and count what you need; the amount means what the table says. Listeners run on the thread that reported: keep them quick and thread-safe. java Copy PlayerActions.listen((player, action, amount) -> { switch (action) { case PlayerActions.CRATE_OPEN -> ...; // a constant on PlayerActions case "jobs_level" -> ...; // the other plugins' actions are plain strings default -> { } } }); Action From Fires when Amount slot_spin ( PlayerActions.SLOT_SPIN ) Slots A slot machine spin The bet slot_win ( SLOT_WIN ) Slots A win, paid or dropped as coins The winnings slot_jackpot ( SLOT_JACKPOT ) Slots A jackpot (also reported as a win) The winnings lottery_tickets ( LOTTERY_TICKETS ) Lottery Tickets bought How many lottery_win ( LOTTERY_WIN ) Lottery A lottery win The prize shop_buy ( SHOP_BUY ) Shop Bought from the shop What it cost shop_sell ( SHOP_SELL ) Shop Sold to the shop What it paid daily_reward ( DAILY_REWARD ) Coins A daily reward claimed The reward pay ( PAY ) Coins A payment to another player What was paid crate_open ( CRATE_OPEN ) Crates A crate opened What it cost (0 when free) quest_complete ( QUEST_COMPLETE , API 5) Quests A quest or achievement finished The reward paid, 0 if none contract_deliver ( CONTRACT_DELIVER , API 5) Contracts Items delivered to a contract or server order How many items coinflip_bet ( CoinflipAPI.ACTION_BET ) Coinflip A stake put into a room The stake coinfl

sections.text: java Copy CasinoSettings.register(new SettingsTab("Dragons", List.of( Setting.heading("Bounties", "What players earn for dragons."), Setting.number("Bounty", 0, 1_000_000, 0, () -> config.bounty, v -> config.bounty = (long) v) .hint("Per dragon.").preview(() -> Message.raw("= " + Currency.format(config.bounty))), Setting.toggle("Announce kills", () -> config.announce, v -> config.announce = v), Setting.text("Chat tag", true, () -> config.tag, v -> config.tag = v).icon("Weapon_Sword_Iron").caption("Tag"), Setting.color("Colour", () -> config.tagColor, v -> config.tagColor = v).inline() ), config::save)); Your tab appears in /tempest for admins (permission tempest.admin ), up to 40 settings (250 from API version 27, SettingsTab.MOST_SETTINGS : a table of rows, each a dropdown with shownWhenChosen fields, as Tempest Claims' perk table). A list of items kept as one text value ("Ingredient_Bar_Iron x16, Food_Bread x5") can show as an item list with ItemRows.of("Milestone items", 6, true, c::getItems, c::setItems) (API 27; from API 28 one "add an item" dropdown with the items under it, each with its count and an X to take it out).
